paragraphs: JX'^VilOG reflected thus, that foremost of Vipras endowed with fleet vigor, bent his steps towards the abode of Yama, for the purpose of relating to him all that had taken place. And there (he) saw that god — Yama — sitting in front of fire and offering into it the good and evil fruits of their actions. f And seeing the Maharshi Narada arrive there, Yama offering him arghya according to the ordinance, addressed him saying, when he was seated at his ease : ‘O Devarshi, Explains the commentator ; ‘ Time hath every thing under its control. Like the all-enclosing space, time pervades .all th.at is. This being so, resorting what transcending Time, shall RAvana obtain victory over it. ’ t Ordaining happiness and misery to the lives ol people .according to IJTTARVKANDAM. is it well with thee ?

And doth virtue deteriorate.'* And, why, O thou honored of deities, and Gandharvas, dost thou come ?’ Thereat the reverened sage, Narada, said ; Hearken. I shall tell (thee) ; and (after hearing me out) do thou what is fit. O king of the Pitris, here cometh the nightranger named ten- necked, for bringing thee under his sway — ^thee who art incapable of being conquered. And, O master, for this reason it is that I have come hither hastily, — doubtful what shall befall thee who hast the rod for thy weapon. In the meanwhile they saw the Raksha’s car approach from afar, flaming and like unto the rayfurnished (one) risen. And dispelling the gloom of that region with the effulgence of Pushpaka, that exceedingly powerful (Rakshasa) came forward.

And the mighty-armed ten-necked one all around saw creatutes reaping the consc qucnccs of their fair and foul acts. And there he saw Yama’s soldiery along with Yatna’s followers, fierce-forms, grim-visaged and terrific. And he saw coporeal beings undergoing torments and pain, and emitting loud cries and sharp shrieks ; preyed on by worms and fell dogs : and uttering words capable of striking pain and terror into the heart (of the hearer) : and people swimming in the Vaitaraini profusely running blood ; and momentarily burning with hot sands ; unrighteous wights pierced in a wood of asipatra^ (plunged) in Raurava, in the river of borate of soda ; and (cut) with razor-edges ; asking for drinks ; and afflicted with hunger and thirst ; converted into corpses, lean, woe-begone, and pallid with hair flowing loosely ; having dust and filth (on their bodies), an i running about distressfully with dry forms; — on the very reverse what Narada intends to say.

He says : ‘Doth religion deteriorate ?’ — i.c. '1 hope, religion doth not deteriorate.’ This is an idiom and natural usage accounts for it, although that usage must in the natuie 01 i 620 RAM AY AN A. the way saw Ravana by hundreds and by thousands. And Ravana also saw some in front of houses engaged in merrymaking with songs and strai ns of instruments, — as the fruit of their pious acts ; and (saw) the giver of kine regailing themselves with milk ; the dispenser of rice, feeding on the same, the bestower of abodes, enjdying mansions, as the fruit of their several acts ; and persons living with damsels decked with gold and gems and jewels ; and other pious folks, flaming in their native energy, all these saw Ravana lord of Rakshasas.

And by his might that mighty one delivered those that w^ere being tormented by their wicked acts. And on being liberated by that Raksha — the ten-necked one, those creatures in a moment began to enjoy their release, that had come to them without thought or suspense. And on the dead being delivered by the magnanimous Rakshasa, the guards of the dead, getting enraged, rushed at the Rakshasa sovereign. And there arose a mighty tumult from all sides ; from the heroic warriors of the king of righteousness rushing (all around.) And those heroes by hundreds and by thousands assailed (Pushpaka) wdth pranas, and bludgeons, and darts and maces, and spears and toviaras. And swiftly sw%arming like bees, they began to break the seats, blocks, daises and gatew^ays (of the car.) And in that conflict Pu.shpaka presided over by divine energy, incapable of being destroyed by virtue of Ikahma power, being broken, resumed its -former shape.

Countless were the soldiers of that high-souled one consisting hundreds and thousands of heroic warriors, (ever) forward for fight. And according to the measure of their might his (Havana’s) ’C ouncillors — great heroes all, as w'ell as the ten-faced one himself with might and main, faught wdth trees and crags and hundreds of blocks of buildings. And those councillors of the lord of Rakshasas, assailed w'ith every kind of weapons, with their persons bathed in blood, faught fiercely. And O largearmed one the exalted councillors of Yaina and Ravana sore assailed each other with arms. And leaving the councillors alone the highly powerful warriors of Yama rushed against Da^anana* with a show'er of spears. And then pierced through and through by those weapons, with his person covered with blood, the Rakshasa king appeared like a flowering Kin^uka in Pushpaka.f And thereat that powerful one, by virtue of his mastery over weapons, began to hurl darts and maces, prdgas and spears and tomaras and crags and trees.

And that terrific shower of trees, rocks and arms, alighted on the army of Yama (fighting) on the earth. And snapping those \veapons and resisting (those volHes of) arms, they smote at the Rakshasa fighting alone by hundreds and thousands. And encompassing him even as clouds encompass mountain, they, rendered (R§.vana) inert by means of Bhindipdlas and darts. And with his mail torn open, his anger raging fiercely, and covered with blood streaming over his person, he, forsaking his car, stood upon the ground. And then furnished with his bow and holding his shafts, (Ravana) regaining his senses in a short time, increased in energy and stood in the field like the finisher. And now fixing the divine Pa^upata on his bow, and saying unto tliem, ‘slay ! slay !’ he drew that bow.

And enraged, (Ravana) resembling Rudra himself, in fight drawing his bow to his car, discharged that shaft even as Sankara had discharged at Tripura. And the appearance of the shaft was like an extinguishing fire in summer with smoke wdth flames, burning up a forest. And garlanded with glory that shaft t This simile is peculiarly appropriate and beautiful. Pushpaka, the nameof Ravana’s car, means composed of flowers; and this signification shining askance, as it were, over the direct sense of the sentence, heightens the delight the reader feels on iinaginging the principal figure. ‘Ravana seated in-. i 622 RAM AY AN A. followed by ghosts,^ in that encounter ; rushed on, burning to ashes the loose bushes and trees lying in its way.

And burnt up by its energy, the most of Vaivasvvata fell down in the field like unto banners of Mahendra. And thereat the RSlkshasa of terrific prowess along with his councillors began to set up tremendous shouts ; as if making the earth tremble.

verses.sa:
एवं सञ्चिन्त्य विप्रेन्दो जगाम लघुविक्रमः ।
आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति ॥

अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम् ।
विधानमुपतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम् ॥

स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम् ।
अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः ॥

कच्चित्क्षेमं तु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति ।
किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित ॥

अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः ।
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम् ॥

एष नाम्नो दशग्रीवः पितृराज निशाचरः ।
उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रमैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम् ॥

एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो ।
दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति ॥

एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दुरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम् ।
ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः ॥

तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः ।
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ॥

सो ऽपश्यत्स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः ।
प्राणिनः सुकृतं कर्म भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम् ॥

अपश्यत्सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह ।
यमस्य पुरुषैरुग्रैर्घोररूपैर्भयानकैः ॥

ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च क्लिश्यमानांश्च देहिनः ।
क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् ॥
कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः ॥

क्षोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः ।
सन्तार्यमाणान्वैतरणीं बहुशः शोणितोदकाम् ॥

वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान्मुहूर्मुहुः ।
असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान् ॥

रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि ।
पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान्क्षुधितानपि ॥

शवभूतान्कृशान्दीनान्विवर्णान्मुक्तमूर्धजान् ।
मलपङ्कधरान्दीनान्रूक्षांश्च परिधावतः ॥

ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।
कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः ।
प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद्रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः ॥

गौरसं गोप्रदातारो ह्यन्नं चैवान्नदायिनः ।
गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः ॥
सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलङ्कृतान् ॥

धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान्स्वतेजसा ।
ददर्श सुमहाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ॥

ततस्तान्भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः ।
रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाद्बली ॥

प्राणिनो मोचितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा ।
सुखमापुर्मुहूर्तं ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम् ॥

प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा ।
प्रेतगोपाः सुसङ्क्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन् ॥

ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः ।
धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां सम्प्रधावताम् ॥

ते प्रासैः परिघैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः ।
पुष्पकं समवर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः ॥

तस्यासनानि प्रासादान्वेदिकास्तोरणानि च ।
पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव ॥

देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे ।
भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥

असङ्ख्या सुमहत्यासीत्तस्य सेना महात्मनः ।
शूराणामग्रयातऽणां सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥

ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा ।
ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम् ।
अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः ॥

ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः ।
अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत् ॥

अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणैर्भृशम् ।
यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः ॥

अमात्यांस्तांस्तु सन्त्यज्य यमयोधा महाबलाः ।
तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्षैर्दशाननम् ॥

ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः ।
फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः ॥

स तु शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् ।
मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली ॥

तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम् ।
यमसैन्येषु तद्वर्षं पपात धरणीतले ॥

तांस्तु सर्वान्विनिर्भिद्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च ।
जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः ॥

परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मोघोत्करा इव ।
भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमपोथयन् ॥

विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिक्तः शोणितविस्रवैः ।
ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत ॥

ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्तत ।
लब्धसञ्ज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः ॥

ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं सन्धाय कार्मुके ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं विचकर्ष स ॥

आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे ।
मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शङ्करो यथा ॥

तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत्विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् ।
वनं दहिष्यतो घर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः ॥

ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे ।
मुक्तो गुल्मान्द्रुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति ॥

ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु ।
रणे तस्मिन्निपतिता दावदग्धा नगा इव ॥

ततस्तु सिचवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः ।
ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम् ॥
